newsitem.title: SWEDEN: DUTCH STATE TO RETAIN SMALL PART OF NEDCAR-VOLVO.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH STATE TO RETAIN SMALL PART OF NEDCAR-VOLVO.

text.p: The Dutch government may hold onto a small stake in car plant, NedCar, Volvo Car vice president Sven Eckerstein said on Thursday.
"The Dutch state might be left with a small part of NedCar," Eckerstein told a transport conference.
"It is not certain that it will sell all of its stake. This is one element of the discussions that NedCar's owners are now having. There is no final date for making a decision on this."
NedCar is currently owned in three equal parts by Swedish vehicle maker Volvo, Japan's Mitsubishi and the Dutch state.
Last summer it was reported in the Netherlands that the Dutch state was considering getting rid of its stake in NedCar, but to date the ownership has not changed.
In connection with this report, Volvo Car said that it would make use of its option to increase its holding to 50 percent of NedCar.
